evidence_basis: 🔴 THIS RECEIPT CLEARS NO READING DEBT AND IS FILED PRECISELY SO THAT NOBODY LATER MISTAKES IT FOR ONE. An abstract is not a reading. It is recorded because 47 citations across 7 canonical files rest on this paper and the state had no receipt of any depth for it — so the honest floor is to say exactly what was consulted.

RETRIEVAL: EXHAUSTED, AND STATED AS A ROUTE RATHER THAN A PROPERTY. Neurogenetics 19(3):151-156, Springer. Europe PMC: pmcid null, inPMC N, inEPMC N, isOpenAccess N, hasPDF N, only a subscription DOI link. NCBI idconv: 'Identifier not found in PMC'. Unpaywall on 10.1007/s10048-018-0549-5: is_oa false, oa_status closed, has_repository_copy false, oa_locations empty. No local artifact. I could not retrieve it by these routes; that is not the same as saying it cannot be retrieved. Whoever has Springer access should take it — it is the highest-yield single retrieval in this queue.

🔴 SO THE 47 CITATIONS ARE NOT ANYONE'S OVERSIGHT: THE PAPER WAS NEVER AVAILABLE TO WHOEVER CITED IT. The datum entered the model from the abstract, which is where it lives. That reframes the finding I filed an hour earlier under DL-META-091: the question is not who skipped a reading, it is what an abstract-sourced premise is allowed to be labelled.

WHAT THE ABSTRACT ACTUALLY STATES, VERBATIM, ON THE POINT THAT MATTERS: 'Functional studies showed normal levels of WWOX transcripts but absence of WWOX protein.' And on mechanism: 'This could be explained by the functional data indicating an impaired translation or premature degradation of the WWOX protein.' TWO alternatives, unresolved by the authors themselves. And on scope: 'Functional WWOX analysis was performed in fibroblasts of one patient' — of two related patients — with 'Transcription and translation were assessed by quantitative real-time PCR and Western blotting'.

🔴 THE STATE HANDLES THIS BETTER THAN I EXPECTED, AND THAT IS THE CORRECTION. disease_model.md records a MAJOR baseline reversal (WM v2.1 -> v3.0, 2026-07-14) that WITHDREW the equation 'normal mRNA + absent protein = post-translational degradation', citing Johannsen's two alternatives. DL-MECH-034 carries 'cause ∈ {impaired_translation, insolubility, premature_degradation} non discriminata'. It also records that absence on a western is a sensitivity limit and not an absolute zero, that a fibroblast is not a neuron, and that Johannsen never tests whether restabilised protein would be functional. A premise imported from an abstract was qualified better than many imported from complete reads.

🔴 THE DEFECT THAT REMAINS IS THE EVIDENCE CLASS, NOT THE CONTENT, AND IT SITS ON A REJECTION. dismissal_ledger DIS-003 — 'Boosting WWOX expression' -> REJECTION THAT HOLDS — names its load-bearing premise as 'Johannsen 2018 — normal transcript, protein absent in fibroblasts homozygous for Gln230. PREMISE: DATO (direct measurement, exact variant)'. `direct measurement` asserts an act — consulting the primary source — that nobody here performed. Rejections are the asymmetric class: a false positive gets tested and dies, a false negative is silent, permanent and self-reinforcing. Proposed reclassification, NOT applied because it touches a canonical rejection: `PREMISE: DATO — abstract-only, primary source never retrieved`, with the rejection itself left standing.

TWO SMALL DRIFTS THAT ONLY THE ABSTRACT MAKES VISIBLE, both of the kind a DATO label hides. The functional work is in fibroblasts of ONE patient of two, and the state states no n. And the authors give TWO mechanistic alternatives while the ledger writes THREE, adding `insolubility` — a defensible addition, since an insoluble species disappears from a soluble-fraction western, but not what the author says, and it sits in a causal statement beside the citation.

🔴 AND A THERAPEUTIC CONSEQUENCE OF THE `impaired translation` ARM THAT I CANNOT FIND STATED ANYWHERE. If the protein is never synthesised, there is nothing to stabilise. A proteostasis strategy addresses only one of the two authorial arms. DIS-003 rejects boosting expression BECAUSE the bottleneck is downstream of transcription — but 'downstream of transcription' and 'stabilisable' are not the same thing, and if the bottleneck were translation the rejection would be right for one reason and wrong for the other. The only thing that settles it is the western nobody has seen: how many lanes, what loading control, what exposure, whether the signal is absent or below threshold, and whether the qRT-PCR used a single amplicon.

WHY THIS IS FILED AT ALL RATHER THAN LEFT AS A FAILED RETRIEVAL. The receipt records the routes and the date, so the next actor re-tests instead of inheriting a verdict.

THE QUESTION THIS RUN WAS FOR: what exactly is the metabolic evidence behind DL-MECH-034, which grades it DATO and treats it as closing the caveat that the Warburg phenotype had never been seen in WWOX-deficient neural tissue. The answer, verbatim and verified: 'Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis of the top 3,000 differentially expressed genes' revealed 'inhibition of processes related to ATP synthesis‐coupled electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation', and 'marked enrichment was seen in pathways related to regionalization, neuron fate commitment and specification, axis specification (ventral–dorsal and anterior–posterior), and glycolysis and gluconeogenesis'. The words Warburg, lactate, Seahorse, OXPHOS, metabolomics and ketogenic appear ZERO times in the body; glycolysis appears once, in the sentence quoted.

✅ AND THE STATE ALREADY CARRIED THE OBJECTION I ARRIVED WITH. DL-MECH-034 states 'Belief: alto sul dato trascrittomico; MEDIO sul salto trascrittoma→flusso metabolico (l'espressione genica non è il flusso: servirebbe Seahorse/fluxomica)', gives the n (WT n=2, KO n=4), names the technique as transcriptomics rather than Seahorse, and cross-links DL-BIO-008, the unresolved lactate contradiction. Second time tonight that a premise I flagged turned out to be better handled than my alarm implied — the first was Johannsen. Recording both is the point: an alarm kept beside its correction is worth more than one deleted.

🔴 WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING, AND IT IS IN THE TITLE OF THE SECTION THE DATUM COMES FROM. That section is called 'Cerebral organoid RNA sequencing revealed major differentiation defects', and the glycolysis enrichment sits inside a list of DEVELOPMENTAL pathways — regionalization, neuron fate commitment, axis specification. Neural progenitors are glycolytic and maturation shifts cells toward oxidative phosphorylation, so a developmentally delayed tissue produces OXPHOS-down / glycolysis-up FOR THAT REASON. The metabolic signature is therefore confounded with the immaturity the paper's own thesis asserts, and the two are not separable from these data. PREMISE: DEFAULT_FROM_TEXTBOOK on the unwritten premise that this transcriptome reflects a WWOX-dependent metabolic setting.

🔴 AND THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT CHANGES WHAT SOMEONE SHOULD DO. DL-MECH-034 rightly names Seahorse OCR/ECAR on WWOX-KO organoids as the discriminating experiment. But a Seahorse run on KO against WT organoids at the same culture week would REPRODUCE THE CONFOUND: if the knockouts are developmentally younger, the assay measures immaturity and reports it as metabolism. The experiment has to be matched for differentiation STAGE rather than for culture age — normalised on maturation markers, or run on sorted populations rather than whole organoids. What would falsify the confound and support DL-MECH-034: the same signature persisting after stage-matching, or the same signature in a WWOX-deficient system with no differentiation defect — which is exactly what the MEF and cancer models of DL-MECH-020 provide, making that corpus more probative here than the current entry implies, not less.

WHAT THIS RUN DID NOT DO, LISTED SO NOBODY INHERITS A FALSE IMPRESSION. Abstract, introduction, methods, discussion and references not read. Figures inspected as CAPTIONS ONLY — no figure image was fetched and no panel was looked at, which is why coverage.figures says captions_only and why this receipt cannot be and is not a complete read. The nine supplementary elements (Appendix, Expanded View Figures PDF, Tables EV1-EV5, Review Process File) were not retrieved; the Appendix Fig S3A/B is where the GSEA/GO output actually lives, so even the metabolic finding rests on the running text's description of a panel I have not seen.

evidence_basis: DECLARED PARTIAL BECAUSE THE PANELS WERE NOT INSPECTED. All 39 panels were accounted for by reading their captions and the running text was read end to end, but no figure image was fetched and no blot was looked at, so coverage.figures is captions_only and this is not a complete read. Methods and references not read either. The manifest names where that gap bites: the K274R result is a blot whose reading is 'was not ubiquitinated', and a densitometry-free negative on a western is exactly the class where a panel changes a conclusion.

🔴 THE PANEL BUDGET WAS COUNTED BY READING THE CAPTIONS, AND THAT WAS A CORRECTION TO MY OWN METHOD. Figure 1 A-F, Figure 2 A-D, Figure 3 A-F, Figure 4 A-F, Figure 5 A-G, Figure 6 A-F, Figure 7 A-D = 39 panels across 7 figures. Three successive ad-hoc scripts had returned 7, then 9, then 6 for this same article, each by a matcher that failed and substituted a plausible small number. `figures_present` derived from the paper means read the captions; it never meant wait for a parser that can count. The budget is a means, not a gate — and I had briefly turned it into one.

🔴 THIS IS THE ARTIFACT WHERE THE EXTRACTOR DEFECT IS TOTAL, WHICH IS WHY THE PER-ARTIFACT TEST IS NOT CEREMONY. Under this branch's extractor the surface yields 0 of 32 figure citations and 2 of 31 occurrences of PPXY; under the fixed one it yields 30 and 31. Building spans here against my own branch would have meant selecting quotes to avoid the vocabulary of a paper titled 'Characterizing WW Domain Interactions'. Spans were built against the correct surface and all 13 then verified under BOTH extractors unchanged.

🔴 THE PREMISE IS CLOSED FROM ITS PRIMARY SOURCE. DL-MECH-083 rests on PMID 25331887 importing K274 and ITCH without demonstrating either. Here they are demonstrated: mass spectrometry identified Lys-100 and Lys-274 as ubiquitinated, and site-directed mutagenesis separated them — 'the WWOX-K274R mutant was not as compared with the WWOX-WFPA construct', while 'ITCH could still ubiquitinate the WWOX-K100R mutant, although to a lesser extent'. Conclusion in the authors' words: 'these data suggest that ITCH predominantly mediates polyubiquitination of WWOX at Lys-274'. Note the comparator — K274R is judged against the WW1-dead construct that cannot bind ITCH at all, so the claim is that it behaves like a non-binder. And note the qualifier: predominant, not exclusive.

THE LINKAGE CALL IS DOUBLY CONTROLLED, WHICH IS UNUSUAL ENOUGH TO RECORD. 'ITCH-mediated WWOX ubiquitination is predominantly Lys-63-linked', established with linkage-specific antibodies whose specificity was itself validated on a protein with established K48-linked proteasomal degradation, and then confirmed orthogonally with ubiquitin constructs 'that are either Lys-63 only or Lys-48 only (all other lysines are mutated to arginines)'. Antibody and genetics agree. This is the primary measurement underneath this repository's own D-01 entry in DEFAULTS THAT BIT US — 'polyubiquitination → proteasome' — which had never been read here from its source.

🔴 AND THE DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE THING THE CANONICAL STATE DOES NOT CARRY ANYWHERE. Cycloheximide chase: 'Expression of ITCH in the presence of CHX extended the half-life of WWOX as compared with CHX alone'. Loss of function: 'We found that WWOX levels were decreased in Itch[-/-] mouse embryonic fibroblasts' and 'WWOX half-life is shorter in the absence of ITCH', p < 0.001. Discussion: 'ITCH ubiquitinates WWOX independent of degradation' and 'coexpression of WWOX and ITCH stabilizes WWOX levels'. ITCH is a POSITIVE regulator of WWOX abundance, in overexpression and in knockout, by level and by half-life.

🔴 WHAT THE STATE SAYS TODAY, AUDITED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. ITCH appears 18 times across the canonical files. DEFAULTS THAT BIT US carries the K48/K63 distinction; DIS-001 was reopened on exactly this biology and correctly advises against inhibiting ITCH, since that would strip WWOX of its DDR function via ATM and Itch-null mice are autoimmune. Every one of those statements treats ITCH as something one might INHIBIT. None records that ITCH ACTIVITY RAISES WWOX ABUNDANCE. The state knew the linkage and the site — third time tonight it was ahead of me — and did not know the sign.

🔴 THE CONSEQUENCE, AND IT CONVERGES TWO OPEN PREMISES ONTO ONE EXPERIMENT. DIS-003 rejects 'boosting WWOX expression' BECAUSE the bottleneck lies downstream of transcription. ITCH-mediated K63 ubiquitination is a downstream handle on WWOX abundance — precisely the arm that rejection leaves open. Whether it is on-target for the reference genotype depends on the disjunction DL-META-091 could not resolve: if Q230P protein is absent through PREMATURE DEGRADATION, a stabilising lever is on-target; if through IMPAIRED TRANSLATION, there is nothing to stabilise. So the western that discriminates translation from degradation on Q230P fibroblasts — already the highest-yield retrieval in the queue as the Johannsen PDF — ALSO decides whether ITCH is a lever. Two premises, one measurement. INFERENZA, and it is a hypothesis for the ledgers, never a candidate treatment.

🔴 A CAPTION THAT CANNOT NAME THE PANEL CARRYING THE RESIDUE THE WHOLE PREMISE RESTS ON. Figure 5's legend announces the two MS/MS spectra as panels 'E and F' and then labels them '(C)' and '(D)' — labels already assigned earlier in the same caption to the ITCH-mutant blot and the Coomassie pull-down — before adding '(E)' for the ion colouring. Four labels for two spectra, two of them reused. The running text resolves it by citing 'Fig. 5, E and F', so the finding is safe; a reader following the legend to the K274 spectrum is sent to a blot of something else. Counting panels by reading the captions is what put this in front of me; a parser would have counted seven letters and passed over the collision.

🔴 THE EXTRACTOR DIVERGENCE WAS MEASURED BEFORE A SINGLE SPAN WAS CHOSEN, AND IT MATTERED ELSEWHERE. This branch does not carry Plan's inline-join fix (2e6fd6a lives on evidence-index and is NOT in main). 🔴 THE PAPER CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE n OF ITS ONLY HUMAN EXPERIMENT, AND THE FIGURE SIDES WITH THE SMALLER NUMBER. Methods: 'We obtained samples of brain tissue from a control male fetus at the 21th gestational week'. Results: 'A parietal section of the cerebral cortex of three fetuses of the same gestational period (sampled as above)'. Figure 2's caption: 'compared to a normal fetus (left panel)'. Every panel of Figure 2 has exactly two columns, Ctrl and II.3 — one control field per stain. So two of three statements and the panel itself say one control; the Results say three. n=1 against n=3 is the difference between a case observation and a small series, on the sole human neuropathological comparison in the paper.

🔴 THE LARGEST EFFECT IN THE PAPER IS REPORTED AS THE PHRASE 'ALTERED DISTRIBUTION'. The BrdU birth-dating experiment gets one sentence: 'we found altered distribution of BrdU-positive cells in lde/lde cerebral walls, revealing delayed migration of late-born neurons'. Panel 3J, read at 3x from the native 1465x1600 JPEG, carries significance markers on EIGHT OF TEN zones — ** at zones 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and * at zones 4, 9, 10 — with zone 2 running from roughly 810 BrdU+ cells/mm2 in wild type to roughly 70 in lde/lde, an order of magnitude. The text gives no number, no direction and no count. Meanwhile the Satb2 result the Results DO foreground is a change of about a third (panel 3G, area 1: ~1830 to ~1230, two asterisks total). The paper's emphasis is inverted relative to the effect sizes in its own panels.

🔴 WHERE THE STOP CODON FALLS DECIDES WHAT THE DISEASE MECHANISM IS, AND NOBODY MEASURED IT. The Discussion states an unresolved disjunction — 'resulting in a loss of normal Wwox function either through protein truncation (and disruption of the active C-terminal short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase SDR domain), or nonsense-mediated mRNA decay' — with no western blot and no transcript quantification. Panel 1G places p.R264Ter in red at the C-terminal boundary of MTS, immediately before the Loop and the Catalytic Site. INFERENZA: if the transcript escapes NMD the product retains WW1, the NLS, WW2, the NADP site and the ENTIRE mitochondrial targeting sequence, losing only the catalytic site and everything C-terminal to it — a catalytically dead Wwox that can still reach mitochondria and still present both WW domains to PPXY partners. Absence and a dead-but-present interactor are different mechanisms with opposite therapeutic implications: one cannot be stabilised, the other might not want to be. PREMISE: DEFAULT_FROM_TEXTBOOK — that a nonsense variant equals a null. This is the same premise Oliver's null/missense classification rests on (PMID 36779245, read 2026-08-10), and it is unmeasured there too.

🔴 THE SAME PANEL INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS THE P47 FINDING FROM OLIVER 2023. Panel 1G, titled as the map of WOREE-associated mutations, carries p.P47R in WW1; the Discussion, four paragraphs later, names p.Pro47Thr and p.Gly372Arg as the two SCAR12 hotspots. Same residue, two substitutions, two different diseases — mild SCAR12 and severe WOREE. This converges on PMID 36779245 ('the more conservative change to threonine was found in SCAR12') and on PMID 42128308's P47T mouse allele that holds protein at wild-type level while disrupting the WW1 PPXY motif. Severity is substitution-specific, not residue-specific, which is a direct problem for any scheme grading severity by variant CLASS.

🔴 THE SIGNIFICANCE AXIS OF THE ONLY MOLECULAR FIGURE CANNOT BE RECONSTRUCTED. Figure 4's y-axis reads '-Log10 adjusted differential value p'. Its printed gridlines are 0.3, 0.5, 1.0 with non-uniform spacing whose ratio (1.37:1) matches a logarithmic axis (1.36:1) and not a linear one (1.5:1) — so the axis is log-scaled in a quantity that is already a negative logarithm. On the label's plain reading the dashed threshold sits near p=0.15 and the most extreme of 9,404 and 9,318 variables reaches only p≈0.04, which is not a credible p-value distribution for a transcriptome. The Methods say 'P significance was calculated according to NOISeq-sim algorithm', and NOISeq's statistic is a probability of differential expression conventionally cut at 0.8 — almost exactly where the threshold line sits — but points appear above 1.0, which a probability cannot take. Neither reading is consistent. The Discussion's 'significantly reduced expression' therefore rests on a criterion the paper does not let a reader reconstruct. This is a PREMISE_TAG on everything downstream of the tubulin result, not a refutation of it.

🔴 THE ABSTRACT ATTRIBUTES THE TRANSCRIPTOMIC FINDING TO PROGENITORS; THE PANEL SHOWS IT IN NEURONS. The abstract says 'Transcriptomic analyses of Wwox-depleted human neural progenitor cells showed an impaired expression of a number of neuronal migration-related genes'. The Results correctly say neurons. Figure 4 settles it: in the progenitor panel the labelled migration genes — TUBB3, DNM1, TUBB6, MAP6, TUBGCP6, TUBA1B — sit in the grey non-significant cloud or in green below threshold and TUBA1A is blue, while in the neuron panel the same names sit in red above threshold at log2 fold changes from about -1.2 to -4.5. The finding is differentiation-dependent, and the sentence most readers carry away is the one that gets it wrong.

🔴 THE PROTEIN-LEVEL TEST OF THE HEADLINE CLAIM WAS DONE, CAME BACK NEGATIVE, AND NEVER REACHES THE DISCUSSION. A >10-fold TUBA1A mRNA reduction is followed by 'Immunostaining in the WWOX-deficient human brain revealed a slight reduction of tubulin-1-alpha protein, although not significant'. The Discussion then says only 'This showed a significantly reduced expression of several tubulins...' with no mention of the protein result. Same asymmetry as DL-BIO-085: transcript abundance is not a readout of protein and protein abundance is not a readout of function. Here the measurement existed and the negative did not travel. Its panel — Supplementary Figure S3 — could NOT be retrieved, so this negative is recorded from the running text alone.

THE THREE LINES OF EVIDENCE COME FROM THREE UNRELATED SYSTEMS, AND THE MOLECULAR ONE IS NOT NEW. The transcriptome is GSE126075 from Kosla 2019, an shRNA knockdown in H9-derived hNPC by some of the same authors: 'obtained in the experiment of in vitro WWOX silencing in H9-derived hNPC as previously described'. So one human fetus carrying p.Arg264Ter, a rat carrying a 13-bp exon-9 deletion, and an shRNA knockdown in an ESC-derived line — and no molecular work in the genotype the paper is about. Legitimate design, but the transcriptomic figure must never be weighted as independent replication of the histology.

NEGATIVES VERIFIED AGAINST THEIR PANELS RATHER THAN TRUSTED, BECAUSE 'NOT SIGNIFICANT' AND 'NOT TESTED' LOOK IDENTICAL IN PROSE. Panel 3H carries no asterisk on any of its eight zones, so the Tbr1 negative is tested. Panel 3E carries none either: wild type 1.51 mm with a tight error bar against 1.64 mm in lde/lde with an error bar roughly eight times wider. The wall is not thinner — which is what makes the zone-by-zone BrdU redistribution a statement about where cells are rather than an artefact of dividing a shorter wall into ten parts. And the quantitative claims DO verify: >15-fold is log2 -3.91 and the TUBB3 leader line reaches the far-left extreme of the red cluster; MAP2, TUBB2B and the KIF5 family point into the -1.2 to -1.8 band matching their stated 2-3-fold. Recording what verifies is part of the audit, not a courtesy.

n=3 PER GENOTYPE, STATED ONCE IN THE METHODS AND NOWHERE IN THE RESULTS: 'Data from each 3 +/+ and lde/lde rats genotyped by PCR were used for statistical analysis'. Every asterisk in panels 3E, 3G, 3H and 3J rests on three animals per group by Student's t-test, with no correction across the ten zones tested per panel. The order-of-magnitude effect at zone 2 is unlikely to be explained away by this; the single-asterisk markers at zones 4, 9 and 10 are a different matter. The eight-of-ten count should never be quoted without its n.

🔴 AND THE SAME CROP PRODUCED THE READING'S BEST FINDING. Panel 3D-d1: burst frequency is 1.0 at baseline, ZERO under d-APV, about 0.15 under CBX, and ABOUT 2.55 UNDER THE PANNEXIN BLOCKER BB-FCF, rising again to about 2.6 at washout. The Results describe this only as 'the effects were not recapitulated with BB-FCF', and the Discussion as 'had minimal effect on the network excitability in the Wwox S-KO model'. A two-and-a-half-fold point estimate in the opposite direction is not an absence of effect. It carries no significance marker and its error bars are wide, so the honest statement is that the direction was never tested and was described as if it had been. The same Discussion paragraph then keeps a pannexin blocker open as a possible anti-epileptic 'at earlier developmental stages' — which may be right, and which a reader of the prose alone would not know needed checking.

🔴 THE ASTERISK CONVENTION IS INVERTED IN FIGURE 3 AND ORDINARY IN FIGURE 6, INSIDE ONE PAPER. Figure 3's caption states 'd2: * p = 0.0036, ** p = 0.0274' — one star on the smaller p, two on the larger — and the panel agrees with its caption, drawing ** on the comparison the text gives as p = 0.0274. Figure 6's caption reads '* p = 0.04761; ** p = 0.00322', the normal direction. The same two symbols rank significance opposite ways in the same article. This is the class of defect this repository paid for on 2026-08-06, when an unmarked asterisk was the difference between 'not significant' and 'not tested'.

🔴 THE EXCITATORY EFFECT IS SIX PER CENT AND THE INHIBITORY EFFECT IS FIFTY-TWO, AND THE ABSTRACT LISTS THEM THE OTHER WAY ROUND. sEPSC amplitude: control 23.3 ± 12.0 pA against knockout 24.7 ± 13.6 pA — a 1.4 pA separation inside a twelve-point spread. sIPSC amplitude: control 57.3 ± 31.0 pA against knockout 27.5 ± 19.4 pA. Figure 4 shows it without arithmetic: in panels B and F-f1 the excitatory cumulative distributions lie almost on top of one another; in H-h1 the knockout curve is displaced across most of the plot. The Results get the emphasis right — 'favors excitation over inhibition, primarily through an impairment in the amplitude of the inhibitory currents' — and the abstract does not, leading with 'elevated amplitude of excitatory post-synaptic currents'. The gap is between the paper's summary and the paper's own results section.

🔴 THE HETEROZYGOTE BURSTS AT A SIXTH THE RATE AND THE DISCUSSION CALLS IT SIMILAR. Stated slice by slice: '0 of n = 11 slices from 7 S-WT mice; 4 of n = 23 slices from 14 S-HT mice; 36 of n = 42 slices from 24 S-KO mice' — 0%, 17%, 86%. The dose-response conclusion survives; the word does not. IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MOUSE: human heterozygous carriers are the consanguineous parents of every published family and they are clinically well.

🔴 A DOSE-RESPONSE THAT IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS PROPERTIES, FROM TABLE 1. Input resistance: 102.88 wild type, 143.26 heterozygote, 143.03 knockout — the two mutants are indistinguishable and both differ from wild type, so ONE ALLELE ALREADY SATURATES IT. Resting potential and sag instead grade monotonically across all three (-79.25 / -75.51 / -73.62 mV; 1.18 / 2.04 / 2.57 mV), and those are the properties the paper ties to hyperexcitability. INFERENZA: a cellular readout can be fully abnormal in a carrier and still not track the phenotype, which is a direct constraint on any Tier 1/2 biomarker drawn from intrinsic membrane properties.

HETEROZYGOTES ARE POOLED INTO THE CONTROL GROUP UNDER A CONDITION NEVER SHOWN FOR THE POOLED MEASURES. The Methods declare it conditionally: 'Where no significant difference exists between S-HT and S-WT groups, they are occasionally represented as a clustered group (S-CTL) for clarity'. Table 1 marks the heterozygote significantly different from wild type on four intrinsic properties, and S-CTL is used for the whole spontaneous-current analysis of Figure 4E-H, whose captions report knockout against each control genotype separately but never wild type against heterozygote. The bias runs conservative — pooling an abnormal genotype into the control understates the knockout effect — so this qualifies rather than refutes.

Figure 6E prints WT = 1 and Itch-knockout = 0.36 under the blot: a 64% reduction in steady-state WWOX from deleting one E3 ligase, where the text says only 'levels were decreased'. 🔴 TWO p-VALUES FOR ONE COMPARISON. The Methods give the phage-display enrichment as 'p value <2.2E−18 using rank sum test'; Figure 2D prints '7.5591721538234e-12' in its own title, for the same rank-sum test of PWM scores against the proteome. The conclusion is unaffected at either value. Recorded because a statistic appearing twice with two values cannot both times be the one that was computed.

THE MOTIF TREE'S ARITHMETIC. Legend and Methods both give the sets as 240 and 144 proteins and describe each leaf number as 'the number of proteins with the motif'. The leaves sum to 563 and 355 — factors of 2.35 and 2.47. Multiple-motif membership would explain it and is nowhere stated. Recorded as an arithmetic observation, not an error claim.

🔴 THE UBIQUITINATION ASSAY IS 'TREATED OR UNTREATED' WITH A PROTEASOME INHIBITOR AND NO PANEL SAYS WHICH. The Methods state cells were treated or untreated with MG-132 for 4 h; only Figure 6B's legend names MG-132, and that is the HIF1alpha antibody control. So for Figures 5A-G, 6A and 6C the presence of a proteasome inhibitor is not recoverable. That matters here because the paper's central claim is that this ubiquitination is degradation-independent, and an inhibitor changes how much conjugate accumulates. It does not touch the K63 linkage or the half-life results, which are separate experiments; it does mean the ubiquitination blots cannot be compared with one another for conjugate abundance.

Figure 6A shows the K63 blot far stronger than K48 for WWOX+ITCH; Figure 6B's HIF1alpha control behaves as it must, K48-positive and K63-negative; Figure 6C's single-lysine ubiquitin constructs agree. 🔴 A TITLE OF MINE CORRECTED IN APPEND, AND IT IS THE THIRD TONIGHT. The first receipt on this paper said ITCH appears '18 times' in the canonical state and that 'every mention treats it as something to inhibit'. The 18 were LINES in four files I chose; the whole tree holds 175 occurrences in 24 files; the orchestrator measured 46 in 101. Three numbers, three tools, none reproducible. And 'every mention' was a generalisation I had not verified. The substantive claim survives and is now TESTED rather than counted: searching the state for any sentence giving the DIRECTION — ITCH raising WWOX abundance or half-life — returns only text written tonight. The lesson is not to verify more before raising an alarm; it is that the alarm and the finding must be separated in the text, because the title is what travels.

evidence_basis: 🔴 WHY THIS PAPER WAS READ, AND IT IS THE PARITY PRINCIPLE IN ITS PUREST FORM. This laboratory has published ZERO papers on WWOX — measured, not assumed: 'Santini S[au] AND WWOX' returns 0. The paper is about Ataxia Telangiectasia, ITCH and liver injury. It was reached only through the reference list of PMID 25331887, entry 42, and it appears in no WWOX query and in no citing bibliography this corpus holds. Yet its single result is the load-bearing arrow of a WWOX model drawn two papers downstream. A premise under a WWOX schematic, supplied by a group that has never studied the gene.

🔴 THE ANSWER TO THE QUEUED QUESTION: THE DIRECTION HOLDS, THE FIRMNESS DOES NOT, AND THE FIRMNESS GROWS AT EVERY HOP. FT-060 asked whether ATM phosphorylates ITCH directly, whether the effect on ligase activity is measured or inferred, and whether an inhibitory sign would overturn the downstream model. The sign is POSITIVE, so the model's direction survives. But the chain of statement across three papers, each quoted verbatim against a fingerprinted artifact, reads: Santini 2014 — 'Point mutagenesis identified Ser161 as a PUTATIVE ATM-target site' and, for the mechanism, 'Pull down experiments ALLOW TO SPECULATE that S161 phosphorylation destabilizes the inhibitory intramolecular interaction'. Abu-Odeh 2014 (PMID 25331887) — 'After DNA damage, ATM positively REGULATES the ligase activity of ITCH (42)': neutral verb, hedge dropped, citation kept. Hazan 2015 (PMID 27308504), the Author's View — 'Activated ATM PHOSPHORYLATES and positively regulates the ligase activity of ITCH': the specific molecular verb appears for the first time, inside a model figure, AND THE CITATION DISAPPEARS. The claim is firmest exactly where its provenance is thinnest. DL-METH-085 was a two-document observation inside one laboratory; this makes it a three-document chain that crosses laboratories.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MEASURED ABOUT THE PHOSPHORYLATION, stated because the downstream verb 'phosphorylates' claims more than this. There is no phospho-S161 antibody in this paper, no in vitro kinase assay with recombinant ATM, and no mass spectrometry. The evidence is a pan-phosphoserine blot on immunoprecipitated ITCH that an ATM inhibitor reduces — Fig 4A, which contains no ATM-minus lane at all, only plus and minus inhibitor — together with a serine-to-alanine mutant that stops responding to ATM. That is a strong genetic argument for S161 being required, and it is not a measured phosphorylation event at that residue. The authors' own verb for the mechanism is 'speculate'.

AND THE SPECIFICITY ARCHITECTURE IS GENUINELY GOOD, recorded because a reading that only qualifies is not reading. Fig 4 carries three controls in one figure: catalytically dead ITCH-C830A gives no signal under any condition; the decoy mutant ITCH-S430A still responds to ATM; and ITCH-S161A still responds to ΔMEK/JNK1, so the mutant is not simply dead. A residue that loses ATM-responsiveness while keeping JNK-responsiveness is discriminating. NEDD4 as an off-target E3 is the other well-chosen control.

🔴 THREE QUALIFICATIONS THE WWOX MODEL IMPORTS NONE OF. (1) THE ACTIVATION IS A PULSE AND THEN REVERSES: 'an early and transient induction of ITCH autoubiquitination. Later on ITCH activity is down-regulated.' A schematic drawing ATM→ITCH as a standing arrow inside a positive feed-forward loop is drawing a transient as a steady state. (2) IT DOES NOT REACH ALL SUBSTRATES, and the authors say so: 'although ATM modulates ITCH activity it may not modulate the ubiquitination and therefore the stability of all ITCH substrates' — p73 is unchanged. WWOX IS NOT AMONG THE SUBSTRATES TESTED HERE, so carrying the arrow into a WWOX model requires assuming WWOX behaves like c-FLIP-L and c-Jun rather than like p73. (3) THE CHAIN TYPE IS NEVER DETERMINED: no linkage-specific antibody, no single-lysine ubiquitin mutant, no linkage mapping in eight figures — and every measured ITCH output here is DEGRADATION, while the WWOX claim is K63 and stabilisation. Not a contradiction, because the substrates differ; it is the reason the arrow cannot be imported with its outcome attached.

PANEL WORK, AND THE WEAKEST PANEL IS THE ONE CARRYING THE MECHANISM. Fig 6B is the pull-down that supplies the molecular explanation for everything downstream, and it has no quantification, no densitometry, no replicate statistics — nothing in the figure supports the word 'significantly', which there can only mean 'visibly'. Worse, the input works against the claim: the ATM-positive lane shows MORE ITCH in the Input row while the Pull-down row band is at best modestly weaker. More input with similar recovery is a smaller effect than the sentence describes. Recorded as panel_qualifies_text rather than as a contradiction, because incomplete is not false.

A FIGURE MIS-CITATION, WITH cited_panel_check SATISFIED. 'the decrease of c-FLIP-L protein levels is significantly compromised in Atm −/− mice (Fig. 6A)' — but Figure 6A is a HEK-293T transfection blot: ATM ±, ITCH wt or S161A, probed for pS1981-ATM, ATM, ITCH and Tubulin. No mouse, no liver, no ConA, no c-FLIP antibody. The next sentence of the same paragraph cites Fig 8A, which is where the result belongs. Third instance of this class in this corpus after PMID 38182577 Fig 6D and PMID 25331887 Fig 3C, and the first found in a paper outside the Aqeilan laboratory — so it is a property of the literature, not of one group.

MG132 IN EVERY UBIQUITINATION EXPERIMENT, stated by the authors in Results rather than buried in Methods. Correct design for visualising conjugates, and it touches this corpus's D-01 default directly: the paper establishes that ATM raises ITCH's ligase output and does not establish which chain ITCH builds.

🔴 A JUNCTION THIS CORPUS DID NOT HAVE, and it is why this paper is more than a citation repair. A-T is a cerebellar neurodegeneration; the authors close by proposing that Atm deficiency may deregulate Gli-1, an ITCH substrate and a Hedgehog effector downregulated during cerebellar differentiation. WWOX-related disorder includes SCAR12, a spinocerebellar ataxia. ITCH therefore sits between the WWOX-DDR axis this corpus has been reading and a cerebellar axis it has not — found in a paper that never mentions WWOX. Recorded as ESPANSIONE: nothing here measures WWOX, Gli-1 and cerebellum together.

AND A REVERSE LIMB NOBODY DRAWS: 'ITCH overexpression may down-regulate endogenous ATM protein levels independently on proteasome activity (data not shown)'. If true, the positive feed-forward loop has a negative limb absent from every downstream schematic. Recorded as IPOTESI with its evidential status attached — 'data not shown' is not a result, and the point is that a future reading should ask whether it was ever published.

SURFACE PREFLIGHT, THREE ROUTES, AND THE DISAGREEMENT DECIDED THE SURFACE. oa.fcgi: record present, license="none", retracted="no" — an author manuscript deposited without an open licence. Europe PMC fullTextXML 96,812 bytes; efetch db=pmc 92,519 bytes; both with a body, eight figures, 38 references. THE DIFFERENCE IS STRUCTURAL: efetch places all eight <fig> outside <body> (body 29,341 chars), Europe PMC places all eight inside (46,114). Eight caption sentences. Europe PMC declared, following the instruction written into FT-060 before this run began — and caption_census.py was run BEFORE opening, confirming 8/8 in body. On PMID 24308844 the same check would have said 0 of 7 and would have prevented a manifest with no caption locator; here it is what makes the mis-citation finding checkable at all, since the proof is a caption.

🔴 THE FIGURE BUDGET WAS DECLARED BEFORE READING AND WAS NOT MET, and it is written as a shortfall. Target: one locator per figure or a named waiver, 8 figures. Achieved: 3 of 8, with five waivers each carrying its cost — Fig 1 the dose-response and kinase-dead control, Fig 2 the substrate ubiquitination that carries the degradative direction, Fig 5 the residue specificity transferred to substrates, Fig 7 the HepG2 rescue, and Fig 8 the in vivo liver panel that is where the mis-cited result actually lives. The Fig 8 waiver is the uncomfortable one: the mis-citation is established from the captions, which are verified prose, so the finding does not depend on the pixels — but whether Fig 8A shows what the sentence claims is left OPEN rather than closed. A budget revised after the fact to match what was done is not a budget.

🔴 coverage.figures IS RECORDED AS captions_only AND THAT UNDERSTATES THE READING BY THREE FIGURES — said here rather than left to look like carelessness. All eight captions were read in the declared surface and THREE of the eight panels were inspected as images (Figures 3, 4 and 6). 🔴 THE QUESTION THE PAPER WAS OPENED WITH, ANSWERED: ATR IS NEVER MEASURED. The title, abstract and every conclusion speak of ATR checkpoint activation. The antibody list contains CHK1, p-CHK1(S296), p-H2AX, ATM, p-ATM(S1981), KAP1, p-KAP1, p-histone H3, WWOX, GAPDH, HSP90 and lamin — NO ATR ANTIBODY. Searched over the whole body: zero hits for anti-ATR, p-ATR, ATR inhibitor, ATR knockdown, siATR, shATR. The only kinase inhibitor is KU-55933, which inhibits ATM. Every ATR claim is p-CHK1 standing in for ATR, on the authority of the paper's own Introduction sentence. A legitimate proxy; not a measurement of ATR.

🔴 AND THE ONE PERTURBATION DEPLETES WHAT IT MEANS TO SEPARATE. Under a 48-hour ATM inhibitor the text reports that p-CHK1 fell 'as well as ATM and its targets KAP1 and ITCH', and the preceding sentence adds 'Surprisingly, following ATM inhibition WWOX levels were significantly reduced'. Panel 5B at 269 ppi: p-ATM and p-KAP1 blank, ITCH nearly blank, WWOX markedly fainter, while total ATM, KAP1, CHK1 and GAPDH are unchanged and p-CHK1 is reduced but clearly present with its induction flattened rather than erased. INFERENZA: with a 48 h pretreatment, 'ATM-dependent ATR signalling' and 'chronic ATM inhibition depleted ITCH and WWOX' predict the same blot. The Discussion reaches for the same caution — 'ATM inhibition results in pan changes that could affect DDR signalling' — without naming the duration, and the abstract carries the conclusion without the caveat.

🔴 THE SUMMARY FIGURE MARKS THE TITLE'S CLAIM WITH A QUESTION MARK. Figure 6 draws SSB to ATR to ATM to ITCH to WWOX with K63-UB, and two feedback arrows from WWOX: the one to KAP1/CHK2 plain, the one toward CHK1/gamma-H2AX carrying a literal '?'. The paper's own schematic rates the WWOX-to-ATR-effector arm as uncertain while the title states it as a finding.

🔴 THE K274 RESULT THAT REFINES DL-THER-095, AND THE CONTROL IS BEHIND A GATE. Restoring wild-type WWOX rescues checkpoint activation and K274R does not — panel 2C shows p-CHK1 returning in Sh+WWOX and staying blank in sh-K274R. But the same panel shows K274R expressed BELOW the wild-type rescue, so on that panel the failure is confounded with level. The paper says it controlled for this with higher-expressing K274R clones in FIGURE S4, and concludes 'lysine 274 is not only important for WWOX stability but also necessary for WWOX signalling upon DNA damage'. S4 IS BEHIND THE PROOF-OF-WORK GATE AND WAS NOT SEEN. If it holds, an ITCH-mediated stabilising lever is not 'add more WWOX' but 'restore a specific modification' — the difference between a plausible therapeutic direction and a misdirected one, and it currently rests on a panel nobody in this corpus has inspected.

🔴 THE WORD CHECK CARRIED IN FROM FT-062, ANSWERED. This paper summarises PMID 24550385 as 'a target of K63-linked ubiquitination resulting in its stabilization and nuclear accumulation'. K63-linked, stabilization — not 'proteasomal'. So the phrase 'direct ITCH/proteasomal stabilization' that a commit candidate here attributes to PMID 23370280 comes from neither this paper nor 24550385, whose language this sentence reproduces.

🔴 PANEL 4C SHOWS K274R IS UBIQUITINATED WHERE THE TEXT SAYS IT IS NOT. The text reports IR-induced ubiquitination of wild type 'but not the mutated form WWOXK274R'. The blot shows a clear polyubiquitin ladder in every K274R lane — weaker and less induced than wild type, but plainly present — while WFPA is much fainter. That is exactly consistent with PMID 24550385, which called K274 PREDOMINANT and not exclusive with K100 still ubiquitinated at reduced efficiency. 'Not' overstates the panel; the earlier paper's word was the accurate one. AND THIS PANEL IS BETTER CONTROLLED THAN ITS PREDECESSOR: the input anti-GST row is even across all twelve lanes, which is precisely the caveat left open on Figure 5G of 24550385 the day before.

🔴 A LOAD-BEARING CONTROL THE PANEL CONTRADICTS. The rescue of chromosomal stability is interpretable only if the reconstituted WWOX is physiological, and the text asserts 'comparable levels of WWOX expression in WT MEFs and KO-Ad-WWOX-infected MEFs'. Panel 3C shows the adenoviral WWOX far stronger than the wild-type lane at day 2 and still stronger at days 5 and 7. The rescue is real — breaks fall from about 5.7 in KO-AdGFP+APH to about 1.9 in KO-AdWWOX+APH — but it was achieved with supraphysiological WWOX.

THE CLEANEST RESULT IN THE PAPER, WHICH DEPENDS ON NO PROXY: aphidicolin induced '∼2.8 ± 1 chromosomal breaks whereas 5.7 ± 1.7 breaks were detectable in KO-MEFs', confirmed by panel 3B, with most breaks falling in common fragile sites per Table S1 (not seen).

THE INDUCTION IS MODEST AND TRANSIENT, AND ONLY THE PANEL SAYS SO. Figure 1 prints densitometry under every blot: peaks between 1.5 and 3.4 fold, and in two panels the last timepoint falls BELOW baseline — 0.6 at 24 h for UVR in MEFs, 0.3 at 6 h for aphidicolin in HEK293T. The abstract says only that levels 'are induced'.

WHAT THE PANELS DID NOT CHANGE, RECORDED BECAUSE AN AUDIT THAT REPORTS ONLY FAILURES IS NOT AN AUDIT. Panel 2A: p-CHK1 and gamma-H2AX rise with UV in control MCF7 and are blunted in shWWOX, with the WWOX row confirming knockdown. Panel 2B: p-CHK1 higher and earlier in HeLa-WWOX than HeLa-EV under hydroxyurea, WWOX absent from the EV lanes as expected for a WWOX-negative line. Panel 4A/4B: nuclear and cytoplasmic accumulation as described, with lamin and GAPDH confirming the fractionation. Panel 5A: p-ATM co-precipitates with GST-WWOX after IR, UV and HU. All support the text.

🔴 THE ATTRIBUTION THIS CORPUS CARRIES IS ROLE-INVERTED. A commit candidate here cites this paper for 'direct ITCH/proteasomal stabilization'. In the paper, WWOX is NOT ITCH's substrate: it is ITCH's ANTAGONIST, and the protein stabilised is ΔNp63α. Verbatim: 'Altogether, these results suggest that WWOX antagonizes ITCH effect on ΔNp63α and stabilizes its protein levels', and in the Discussion 'we show that WWOX competes with ITCH on binding to ΔNp63α and inhibits ΔNp63α ubiquitination mediated by ITCH and thus increases ΔNp63α protein stability'. Substrate, stabiliser and direction are all inverted.

🔴 AND THE MEASURED ABSENCES MAKE IT CERTAIN RATHER THAN LIKELY. Over the whole body: 'K63' ZERO occurrences, 'Lys-63' ZERO, and no sentence anywhere describes WWOX as ubiquitinated — zero hits for 'ubiquitination of WWOX' or 'WWOX ubiquitination'. What is present is ITCH 26 times, stabilization 8, proteasome 6, and every one belongs to ΔNp63α. A negative measured on several independent probes that agree is stronger than a positive on one.

🔴 SO FT-062'S QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND THE TWO WORDS DO NOT BELONG TO ONE MECHANISM. PMID 24550385 and PMID 26675548 both say K63-linked and degradation-INDEPENDENT for ITCH acting on WWOX; this paper says PROTEASOMAL for ITCH acting on ΔNp63α, and WWOX blocking it. Two substrates, two chain types, two outcomes. Our phrase borrows a real word from a real sentence and reattaches it to the wrong protein.

WHAT DOES NOT MOVE: DL-THER-095. It rests on PMID 24550385 — the cycloheximide chase, the Itch-knockout MEFs, the 0.36 densitometry — which was read on 2026-08-10 and where the measurements are. It never depended on this paper. The correction is to the attribution in the commit candidate, which is another actor's artifact, not to the ledger entry.

🔴 AND THE FRAME THAT RECONCILES THE TWO, WHICH IS THE AUTHORS' OWN: 'WWOX can compete with other WW domain-containing proteins, like YAP and ITCH, for binding common target proteins, such as ErbB4 and p73'. WWOX both IS a substrate of ITCH (K63, stabilising) and COMPETES with ITCH for its other substrates. Both run through WW1 and PY motifs, so both can hold. INFERENZA WITH A THERAPEUTIC EDGE, and neither paper gives it alone: raising ITCH activity to stabilise WWOX would simultaneously increase ITCH-mediated degradation of its other targets — ΔNp63α here, p73 in Figure 7 of PMID 24550385. AN ITCH LEVER IS NOT SELECTIVE FOR WWOX.

The refusal fired correctly while the reason stayed unknown until the captions were read. Fifth instance in two days of one class — a predicate that is plausible, well-formed, and answering a different question from the one asked.

FIGURE SURFACE: THE PAGE, NOT THE STREAM. The PDF holds TEN image fragments at 82-252 effective ppi because this deposit splits each figure across several streams; extracting them would give pieces without their panel labels. Six pages were rendered at 300 dpi instead, which yields each figure as the reader sees it together with its caption. All ten fragments carry smask = 0, so extraction would have been faithful — it would simply have been the wrong unit. The choice is between fidelity and the right object, and here they diverged.

🔴 THE PAPER CONTAINS NO STATISTICAL ANALYSIS AT ALL. Measured over the body: zero occurrences of a statistics section, of any p-value, of t-test, Student, ANOVA, SEM or a stated n. Error bars are labelled STDV in three captions and panel 6d has none. Yet the Results call an eightfold increase in cell death 'significant' and the transactivation suppression 'significant and dose-dependent'. The effects in Figure 6 are large — about 4% dead cells for cisplatin alone against about 14% for WWOX plus doxycycline plus cisplatin — so the direction is not in doubt; what is absent is any test, and the word asserts one.

A FRACTIONATION CONTROL DESCRIBED AS EXCLUSIVE WHEN THE PANEL SHOWS IT IS NOT. The text says 'Successful fractionation was confirmed by the exclusive presence of GAPDH and lamin in the cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions'. In panel 4a GAPDH is visible in all three nuclear lanes and lamin in the cytoplasmic lanes. The reported ΔNp63α shift is visible and is not in question; the description of the control is.

WHAT THE PANELS CONFIRM, RECORDED BECAUSE AN AUDIT THAT REPORTS ONLY FAILURES IS NOT AN AUDIT. Figure 3 supports the whole mechanism: ITCH increases the ΔNp63α ubiquitin ladder and WWOX collapses it; cycloheximide chase shows ΔNp63α maintained with WWOX and decaying with the non-binding Y33R; knockdown lowers endogenous ΔNp63α. Figure 1 shows WWOX co-precipitating with ΔNp63α and not TAp63α across four formats. Figure 2 maps the interaction to WW1 and shows the PY mutant AAxA still binding — the authors' own unexpected result. Figure 5 shows dose-dependent reporter suppression with partial rescue by Y33R. Nothing in the figures contradicts the paper's own account of itself; what it contradicts is our summary of it.

MULTI-HOP DONE RATHER THAN DECLARED OPEN, BECAUSE THE LEDGER REFUSED THE SHORTCUT AGAIN AND IT PAID AGAIN. 66 references, every one carrying a PMID, 6 gene-direct. Three sit queued (17360458, 17575124, 15070730) and THREE ARE NEITHER READ NOR QUEUED: 18487609 (Aqeilan 2008, WWOX essential for postnatal survival and bone metabolism), 16061658 (Aqeilan 2005, WW domain-containing proteins and ErbB4) and 12514174 (Chang 2003, JNK1 physically interacts with WW domain-containing oxidoreductase). The last two matter for the frame of entry 5: they are the earlier instances of WWOX competing at WW1 for partners, which is the mechanism this paper generalises.

🔴 THE TEXT LAYER IS SUSPECT AND IS REFUSED, NOT NORMALISED. Two C0 control characters, and — decisively — ZERO occurrences of <, >, ≤, ≥, ±, ×, −, µ, α, β or Δ across 44,465 extracted characters, in a paper that uses 'significan' six times and reports plasmid amounts throughout. Suspicion by absence: those characters are certainly on the printed page.

🔴 AND THE DAMAGE WAS THEN IDENTIFIED CHARACTER BY CHARACTER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A SCREENING VERDICT. Page 4 reads 'using 63\x01 objective lens' — the control character stands for ×. Page 6 reads '(6.0 Ag)', '(1.0 Ag)', '(7.0 Ag)': THE MICRO SIGN HAS BECOME THE LETTER A, sixteen times, on every plasmid amount in the methods and legends. And seven times the extracted text reads 'p73h' where the paper prints p73β — an ISOFORM NAME silently corrupted — plus 'h-dystroglycan' for β-dystroglycan.

THE SCALE, AND IT MATCHES THE RULE'S OWN ESTIMATE. Twenty-five identified corruptions, of which TWENTY-THREE ARE PRINTABLE — 92%, against rule 5d's 'roughly 80% of the damage is printable, so no control-character check can see it'. A control-character scan would have found two of twenty-five and reported the surface clean.

WHAT WAS CHECKED AND CAME BACK NEGATIVE, RECORDED BECAUSE A SCREEN THAT ONLY REPORTS HITS IS NOT A SCREEN. The comparator signature that bit PMID 33914858 — 'P 5 0.05' — does not occur here: zero matches. And the nine isolated 'D' characters are genuine (FRA16D, panel D, cyclin D1), not corrupted Δ. Checked rather than assumed.

🔴 THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUTE. Rule 5d: a SUSPECT surface is refused and never repaired, because a manual fix across sixteen instances is indistinguishable from a rewrite and verifiable by nothing. There is no structured surface to re-derive from and no cleaner PDF to obtain. So this paper can only be read from the RENDERED PAGE, and any verbatim locator it produces is a rule-5e page adjudication — source-PDF digest, page, crop rectangle in PDF points, dpi, SHA-256 of the image, recorded as a recipe and never as the image. That machinery exists on main (regenerate_adjudications.py) and arrived in this branch with the merge.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE FILE. PMID 16061658 is the origin of the WW1 COMPETITION FRAME — WWOX and YAP competing for ErbB-4 — which PMID 23370280 generalises and on which the inference written yesterday rests: that raising ITCH activity to stabilise WWOX would also increase degradation of its other PY targets, so an ITCH lever is not selective. That inference cites a frame whose primary source cannot currently carry a verifiable quote. The inference is not thereby wrong; it is thereby unanchored, and saying so is the point of this receipt.

AND IT CLOSES NOTHING IN THE MULTI-HOP. FT-062's gate — 'references queued but not resolved' — needed one gene-direct reference resolved to a receipt. This receipt is retrieved_not_read, which is a receipt, so whether it satisfies that gate is a question for whoever runs the check next; it should NOT be assumed to. The honest position is that the reading debt on PMID 16061658 is untouched.

The SAME ARTICLE'S PDF extracts 61,304 characters with 126 C0 controls and ZERO occurrences of < > <= >= ± × − µ α β Δ against twelve uses of 'significan'. 🔴 AND THE PREFLIGHT TOOL ITSELF WAS FOUND DEFECTIVE ON THE FIRST PAPER IT WAS APPLIED TO. The ToUnicode screen handed over this morning is file-level: does the PDF carry any glyph-to-Unicode map. This PDF carries seven and is nonetheless SUSPECT, because the seven belong to the WarnockPro text faces while MathematicalPi-One, MathematicalPi-Four and Universal-GreekwithMathPi — the fonts that set α β × ± µ Δ — have none. THE MAP IS MISSING EXACTLY WHERE THE CHARACTERS THAT MATTER LIVE. Re-measured per-font across all 55 local PDFs: 11 have zero maps anywhere, and 10 MORE have a map while a symbol font lacks one. Three of those ten are SUSPECT by absence — 18487609, 24550385, 26499798 — and 23370280 shows sentinel zero with AdvGreek unmapped. Eleven mines become twenty-one. Reported to the orchestrator for Plan before the tool was written.

AND THE CORPUS WAS AUDITED AGAINST THAT DEFECT AND CAME BACK CLEAN, WHICH IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS. All 36 deepdive manifests were searched for a text surface derived from a PDF. Exactly one exists, PMID42128308_Aqeilan2026_fitz.txt; its PDF re-measured per-font has 14 fonts, ZERO without ToUnicode, sentinel alpha5 beta20 Delta2 and nine angle brackets, zero C0. Everywhere else a PDF is article_binary. Rule 5c held: no locator in this corpus rests on a defective layer. The defect is in the tool being built, not in the state — but it would have entered the state the first time anyone derived a .txt from 24550385 trusting the file-level pass.

🔴 THE FINDING OF CONSEQUENCE: RUNX2 CHANGES SIGN BETWEEN TISSUE AND ISOLATED CELL, IN THE SAME KNOCKOUT, IN THE SAME PAPER. Figure 5A, day-7 bone in vivo: Runx2 in KO reads 1.50 in femur and 1.385 in calvaria against WT at 1.0, while every matrix and differentiation gene falls. Figure 6C, calvarial osteoblasts isolated from day-3 pups and harvested at day 12: Runx2 reads 0.295, a 70% fall. INFERENZA: this is a tissue-versus-cell-autonomous split rather than a contradiction — the tissue measurement includes compensatory recruitment into the osteoblast lineage, which the isolated culture removes.

🔴 AND THE DISCUSSION'S SUMMARISING SENTENCE — THE ONE SHAPED TO TRAVEL — STATES THE DIRECTION ITS OWN FIGURE 5A REFUTES: 'an indirect effect that leads to decreased RUNX2 expression in bone and in isolated osteoblasts'. The 'in isolated osteoblasts' half is right; the 'in bone' half is wrong, and they are joined by 'and' so a reader inherits both. Four hundred words earlier the same Discussion writes 'slightly increased in both calvarial and femoral bone', and the Results write 'increased ∼25%'. The paper states both directions for the same measurement. Anyone building on the take-home sentence builds on the wrong sign.

🔴 THE CONSTRAINT THIS PLACES ON TRACK C, WRITTEN AS A CONSTRAINT AND NOT AS AN OBSERVATION. A NODE WHOSE SIGN CHANGES BETWEEN TISSUE AND ISOLATED CELL CANNOT CARRY A REPURPOSING HYPOTHESIS. Track C requires a signed pathway direction before a node opens; RUNX2 downstream of WWOX does not have a sign, it has one sign per preparation, and any agent chosen to push it would push it the wrong way in one of the two. Same shape as the confound found in PMID 26675548 the same morning, where a metabolic signature and a differentiation defect were carried on one readout.

AND THE MAGNITUDE IS UNDERSTATED BY HALF IN THE RESULTS: the text says ∼25% in both tissues, the panel reads +50% in femur and +39% in calvaria. Recorded separately from the sign error because a reader quoting '25%' propagates a different and smaller error than one quoting 'decreased' — but both originate here. Two further text-panel numeric divergences, both in the flattering direction: 'a 4-4.5-fold stimulation' measures 3.28x on panel 8A (7.48 over a 2.28 basal) and 3.71x on 8B; 'reduced basal activity by ∼50%' measures 60%.

🔴 THE FINDING THIS PAPER WAS RE-OPENED FOR, AND IT STANDS FROM THE FIRST READING. A commit candidate in this repository cites PMID 23370280 for 'direct ITCH/proteasomal stabilization' of WWOX. THE ROLES ARE INVERTED. In this paper ITCH is not acting on WWOX: ΔNp63α is ITCH's substrate, WWOX is the third party, and the authors' own verb for the relationship is that WWOX COMPETES with ITCH for ΔNp63α — reducing ITCH-mediated ubiquitination of ΔNp63α and extending ΔNp63α's half-life. The stabilised protein is ΔNp63α, not WWOX. Substrate, stabiliser and direction were all reversed in the attribution, and it was caught in quarantine before it reached a canonical file.

AND 'PROTEASOMAL' IS NOT THIS PAPER'S WORD FOR WWOX EITHER. The proteasome in PMID 23370280 belongs to the ΔNp63α arm. The claim that ITCH raises WWOX abundance rests on PMID 24550385 — cycloheximide chase in Itch-/- MEFs, 0.36 against 1 — and that is K63-linked and degradation-independent, which is a different chemistry from the word 'proteasomal' the candidate used. So this paper does NOT supply an independent source for DL-THER-095; it supplies the frame that makes DL-THER-095 legible, and the two must not be merged.

THE EPISTEMIC PERIMETER, HELD AS STATED. DATO: WWOX and YAP compete for a shared partner (PMID 16061658, now page-adjudicated). DATO OF THIS SOURCE: WWOX and ITCH compete on ΔNp63α, by direct co-immunoprecipitation with a WWOX-Y33R rescue control. INFERENZA supported by the two together: a therapeutic lever on the WW interaction network risks non-selective effects. NOT a DATO of PMID 16061658: 'ITCH is not selective' — that paper does not manipulate ITCH. And the ITCH absence reported there holds FOR THE FIGURE 6 MODEL, read off the diagram, not as a global absence. Two PPxY contacts against one make the ErbB-4 competition ASYMMETRIC; they do not demonstrate that YAP is hard to displace, and that remains labelled mechanistic inference.

🔴 THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE FT-064 CLASS, FOUND ON THE DAY THE PREDICATE WAS WRITTEN AND BY LOOKING FORWARD. In a thick 3D matrix scaffold, WWOX-silenced human neural progenitors 'remained as isolated, single cells that did not proliferate nor differentiate' while controls built extensive networks. In 2D monolayer, 'No such phenomenon was observed'. One readout, two preparations, opposite answers, and the conclusion carries one. In DL-MECH-096 the axis was tissue versus isolated osteoblast and RUNX2 changed sign; in DL-MECH-094 it was organoid metabolic signature versus differentiation defect. HERE THE AXIS IS CULTURE DIMENSIONALITY — a WIDENING of the predicate rather than a literal match, and the widening is itself the finding: what varies is not only 'tissue versus cell' but any preparation variable that restores or removes mechanical and matrix context.

AND THE 2D PANEL IS NOT QUITE 'NO PHENOMENON', WHICH STRENGTHENS THE POINT RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. Figure 7 shows both genotypes forming MAP2-positive networks in 2D — the paper's claim, and fair — but the silenced panel is visibly sparser, with processes radiating from a few dense clusters and large fields of isolated nuclei. INFERENZA with its own caveat: micrograph field selection can produce exactly that appearance and no 2D network density is quantified anywhere. So the honest reading is that the effect is DIMENSIONALITY-DEPENDENT IN MAGNITUDE rather than present-or-absent — a phenotype whose size is set by the preparation, which is exactly what a repurposing endpoint would have to be chosen against.

AND THE CONTROL THAT WOULD RULE OUT THE OBVIOUS ARTEFACT IS MARKED 'data not shown'. Cells staying isolated in a 3D scaffold is also what too-sparse seeding looks like. The authors state that seeding density made no difference and that the result held across three experiments; neither the density series nor the replicate spread appears in the paper or its supplements. PREMISE_TAG: PREMISE: INFERENZA. Probably right, not evidenced here. REVIVAL_TRIGGER: any 3D density series or a quantified network measure.

A reader taking either number alone concludes something different about where WWOX matters most.

🔴 THE CONVERGENCE THAT ONLY THREE PAPERS IN ONE DAY COULD PRODUCE. The WWOX-dependent leading-edge set in human neural progenitors contains ERBB4, WWTR1 and RUNX2 — respectively the competed-for partner of PMID 16061658 page-adjudicated this morning, TAZ which PMID 18487609 names as the WW protein that ACTIVATES RUNX2 where WWOX represses it, and RUNX2 itself, whose sign inversion between tissue and isolated osteoblast is DL-MECH-096. Three partners established in bone and breast cancer, together in a WWOX-dependent programme in human NEURAL progenitors. INFERENZA with real limits: a leading-edge subset is a ranked-list artefact, not a measurement of any one gene, and nothing here shows WWOX binding any of them in this cell type. What it does show is that the WW/PPxY competition network is transcriptionally live in the tissue the disease is about — the first place in this corpus where the oncology mechanism and the neural phenotype touch the same gene names.

WWOX in whole human brain is HIGHER in adults than in 20-33 week fetuses, 17.7 against 9.2 TPM RLE, and varies strongly by compartment — highest in corpus callosum and medulla oblongata, confirmed on Figure 1. WOREE's most consistent structural finding is corpus callosum hypoplasia, 75% in the Piard cohort read an hour earlier, and this dataset puts WWOX's highest brain expression in the corpus callosum. A correlation between two public datasets and nothing more — but the kind that decides which region a future measurement is taken in.

Absence is exactly what would happen for ANY variant this rare, pathogenic or benign — the observation has no discriminating power. 🔴 THE HUMAN ASSOCIATION DOES NOT REACH GENOME-WIDE SIGNIFICANCE, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO. The conventional threshold is 5e-8; the two lead SNVs are 1.11e-7 and 2.05e-7 — two to four times above it. The abstract reports both p-values without qualification and the title asserts the association. Not concealed; placed where fewest readers go. Their second stated limitation explains the first: two cohorts of 4,635 and 4,205 are underpowered for a quantitative-trait GWAS, and the fly experiment is offered in place of the power.

🔴 AND THE EFFECT IS ABOUT A QUARTER OF AN HOUR, WHICH NO SENTENCE STATES IN MINUTES. Table 3's betas are in HOURS: minor homozygotes lose 0.209 h at rs16948804 and 0.304 h at rs4887991 — TWELVE AND EIGHTEEN MINUTES, against a cohort SD of 1.4 h, so roughly 0.15 to 0.22 SD. THE UNIT IS WHAT HIDES IT. INFERENZA with a direct bearing on this corpus: an intronic common-variant effect of a quarter-hour in middle-aged adults is a different biological object from biallelic WWOX loss of function, and nothing licenses reading one as evidence about the other. Sleep is a declared axis of the priority matrix, which is exactly why the two must not be merged there.

🔴 AND THE PHENOTYPE IS A QUESTIONNAIRE WITH A DERIVED VARIABLE THAT CANNOT MEAN WHAT IT SAYS. Sleep duration is self-reported for the past month at a 2001-2003 baseline. Habitual sleep efficiency is derived as duration over time in bed and reported as 98.3 ± 12.6%. A MEAN OF 98.3 WITH SD 12.6 ON A QUANTITY BOUNDED AT 100 REQUIRES A LARGE FRACTION OF VALUES ABOVE 100% — participants reporting more sleep than time in bed. Measured efficiency at this age is typically 85-90%. The variable carries none of the paper's claims and Table 3 correctly finds no association with it; recorded so that a corpus later reaching for 'sleep efficiency' from this cohort knows it is reaching for an artefact of self-report arithmetic.

THE FLY RESULT SPLITS BY TIME OF DAY RATHER THAN REPRODUCING THE HUMAN DIRECTION. Daytime sleep falls, night-time sleep rises; the abstract states both honestly. Panel C measures roughly 500 to 300 minutes by day and 500 to 650 by night, so the net is a modest reduction. What 'confirmatory experiments' cannot mean is that the fly reproduced the human phenotype: the human finding is reduced total self-reported duration, the fly gives a redistribution across the light cycle.

🔴 AND THE FIGURE'S OWN TITLE CLAIMS MORE THAN ITS PANEL D SUPPORTS. Figure 2 is titled 'changed sleep duration WITHOUT AFFECTING THE CIRCADIAN RHYTHM', evidenced by panel E — free-running period 23.5 h in both, rhythmicity 96.9% against 96.7%. But panel D shows the mutant's EVENING ACTIVITY PEAK MARKEDLY BLUNTED, about 60 beam counts against the control's 100 at ZT11-12, while the morning peak is far more similar. In Drosophila that evening rise is anticipatory behaviour driven by the clock's evening oscillator, and IT CAN BE LOST WITH AN INTACT FREE-RUNNING PERIOD: period measures the pacemaker, anticipation measures its coupling to behaviour. 'Without affecting the circadian rhythm' is supported for the pacemaker and not for its output. Panel B agrees — the night-time gain is not uniform but concentrated after roughly ZT20, where controls become active and mutants stay at ceiling.

A CHECK THAT CAME BACK NEGATIVE FOR THE PAPER AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. Reduced activity WITH reduced daytime sleep looked incoherent to me, since fly sleep is scored as five minutes without beam crossings and less activity ought to mean more scored sleep. The authors use it to argue against a locomotion artefact and they are right: the resolution is fragmentation, which panel F confirms with reduced daytime average bout length. Short broken activity prevents five-minute quiescent windows without raising total counts. My objection was wrong and the paper had already answered it.

🔴 AND THE SAME PARTNER SET APPEARS A FOURTH TIME TODAY. This paper's one-sentence account of WWOX function names p73, ErbB4, Ap2γ, RUNX2 and HIF1α as WW-domain partners. Those are the partners of PMID 16061658 page-adjudicated this morning (ErbB4, p73, AP-2γ) and PMID 18487609 read this morning (RUNX2), and three of them turned up in the neural-progenitor leading edge of PMID 31543760 an hour ago. It is a review sentence with citations, not a finding of this paper — recorded because FOUR INDEPENDENT PAPERS READ IN ONE DAY CONVERGE ON ONE PARTNER SET, which is the argument for treating the WW/PPxY competition network as the corpus's central mechanistic object rather than an oncology detail.

🔴 THE FINDING THE OPERATOR'S FRAMING WAS ASKING FOR: TWO LARGELY DISJOINT LITERATURES ON ONE GENE, AND THIS CORPUS HAS ONLY EVER READ ONE. Measured on the citation base: 43 of 127 references (34%) share an author with this review and 25 (20%) contain a Chang, against FOUR references to Aqeilan and ONE to Croce. Of the seven papers read here in two days, EXACTLY ONE is cited — O'Keefe 21075834, handed off yesterday. NOT cited: PMID 16061658 (2005, the WW1 competition frame page-adjudicated yesterday), PMID 18487609 (2008, bone and RUNX2), PMID 23370280 (2013, ΔNp63α and ITCH) — all long predating this review and all central to our model. And the WOREE clinical literature is essentially absent: ZERO Piard, Mignot, Repudi or Hussain, in a 2018 review with a section headed 'WWOX in Neurodegeneration In Vivo'. Our state is built on the Aqeilan/Croce axis; this is the Chang axis — Tyr33/Ser14 phosphorylation, Zfra, Hyal-2, bubbling cell death, TIAF1/TPC6AΔ aggregation. Neither is visible from inside the other.

🔴 AND THE CONTRADICTION THAT MATTERS MOST IS ABOUT A FRAME ADJUDICATED YESTERDAY. This review states cytoplasmic sequestration of transcription factors as a property of TRANSIENTLY OVEREXPRESSED WWOX in cancer cells in vitro — and says in the very next sentence that ENDOGENOUS WWOX does the opposite, relocating to the nucleus TOGETHER WITH its partners. FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE FT-064 CLASS, on a new axis: DL-MECH-096 turned on tissue versus isolated osteoblast, DL-MECH-094 on organoid signature versus differentiation defect, PMID 31543760 on 3D versus 2D culture, and this on OVEREXPRESSED VERSUS ENDOGENOUS PROTEIN. Same readout — where WWOX puts its partner — opposite answers, preparation decides.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ADJUDICATION IS BOUNDED AND STATED THAT WAY. PMID 16061658's competition experiment is a co-transfection at fixed and variable plasmid doses — the overexpression condition. ITS DATO STANDS EXACTLY AS ADJUDICATED. What does not follow, and what this corpus must not quietly assume, is that endogenous WWOX at physiological level sequesters ErbB-4 the same way. That is a claim about a preparation nobody in the read set has tested, and it is now named rather than inherited.

🔴 AND IN THIS LITERATURE ACTIVATED WWOX KILLS NEURONS, WHICH INVERTS THE THERAPEUTIC DIRECTION A WOREE MODEL WOULD ASSUME. Our state reasons from loss of function. This review holds both arms: WWOX loss permits protein aggregation, AND Tyr33-phosphorylated WWOX accumulating in the nucleus causes rapid neuronal death after nerve dissection, retinal light damage and MPP+ neurotoxicity. Its Table 1 classifies WWOX in neural injury as 'a pro-apoptotic factor' where the oestrogen receptor is pro-survival. DIRECT BEARING ON TRACK C: 'more WWOX' is not a direction this literature supports, and any node aiming to raise WWOX has to say WHICH SPECIES — the review's own resolution is a BALANCE between pS14-WWOX and pY33-WWOX, not a level. That converts 'how much WWOX' into 'which WWOX', and only the second is tractable.

🔴 A SECOND CONTRADICTION, WITH A PAPER READ YESTERDAY, AND THE REVIEW SUPPLIES ITS OWN RECONCILIATION. Liu states WWOX PROTEIN is significantly increased in human fetal brains; PMID 31543760 read yesterday reports from FANTOM5 that adults exceed 20-33 week fetuses, 17.7 against 9.2 TPM RLE. Opposite directions — and not the same measurand: protein against transcript. The review states the reconciling principle itself, 'gene expression cannot always correlate with protein expression', and demonstrates it at length in skin squamous cell carcinoma where WWOX protein falls with mRNA unchanged. THE CORPUS MUST CARRY BOTH WITH THE MEASURAND ATTACHED: a developmental claim about WWOX in brain is not answerable without saying protein or transcript.

🔴 A Z-SCORE REPORTED AS A FOLD CHANGE, AND THE FIGURE'S OWN CAPTION CONTRADICTS THE TEXT. The narrative claims WWOX expression is upregulated 2.31-fold in the cingulum bundle and 2.78-fold in the central glial substance. Panel 2A's y-axis is labelled Z-SCORE and its cingulum-bundle bar stands at about 2.3 — the number in the text is a bar height on a standard-deviation axis wearing the word 'fold'. Meanwhile that panel's caption sends the reader to Supplementary Table S1 'for WWOX gene expression in the normal brains (AROUND ONE-FOLD CHANGES FOR ALL INDICATED REGIONS)'. Three statements, mutually inconsistent unless the folds are Z-scores. THIRD CONSECUTIVE DAY A QUANTITY HAS CHANGED MEANING WITH ITS PRESENTATION — hours instead of minutes in PMID 39952983, a mean above its own definitional threshold in PMID 30356099, a standard-deviation score called a fold here.

AND THE ANALYSIS IT RESTS ON IS n = 6, STATED TWICE BY THE AUTHORS. Six postmortem individuals with detectable signal. Panels 2B and 2C, by contrast, carry n between 36 and 48 per region with four-asterisk significance — SO THE REVIEW'S WEAKEST ANALYSIS IS THE ONE ITS NARRATIVE LEANS ON and its strongest concerns aged and injured brains. A two-decimal fold change computed on six brains is a precision the sample cannot support, whatever the unit.

PANEL 4E SHOWS A NON-MONOTONIC GENOTYPE SERIES THE TEXT SMOOTHS. The review says pT181-Tau aggregation is 'barely detectable in the wild type and heterozygous Wwox mice'. The quantification puts Wwox+/+ at roughly 10%, Wwox+/− at roughly 5% — BELOW wild type — and Wwox−/− at roughly 28%, with a single p = 0.0176 and NO n stated. A heterozygote below wild type is not a gene-dosage pattern, and one phrase groups two bars that differ twofold. The knockout direction is not in doubt; the series is not a dose-response and should not be read as one.

A NEGATIVE THE REVIEW STATES ABOUT ITSELF, WORTH MORE THAN MOST OF ITS POSITIVES: 'functional interaction between WWOX and CDK5 has never been documented'. CDK5 hyperphosphorylates tau and APP and is an obvious candidate for the mechanism proposed. On a review with a 34% self-citing base, what the authors say is NOT known is the most trustworthy category in it. REVIVAL_TRIGGER: any measurement of WWOX against CDK5 tests the aggregation model at the point its own authors mark untested.

AND THE PARTNER SET SURVIVES A CHANGE OF LITERATURE, WHICH IS STRONGER THAN FOUR PAPERS WITHIN ONE. This review's account of the first WW domain names p73, ErbB-4, SIMPLE, WWBP1, WWBP2, Ezrin, AP-2g and Runx-2 — the same set four independent readings landed on yesterday, reached here through an almost disjoint citation base. Still a review sentence with citations and not a measurement; what it adds is stability ACROSS the two literatures.

evidence_basis: PRIMARY RESCUE OBSERVATION. Stable WWOX re-expression reduced migration/invasion in HOS and LM7 cells and reduced lung-metastasis incidence in five-animal mouse arms after intratibial or intravenous delivery. Ectopic rescue in established cancer lines is mechanistic evidence, not a therapeutic intervention.

THE TITLE OVERSTATES THE RUNX2 EXPERIMENT. Several reported metastasis genes and RUNX2 targets changed with WWOX expression, but RUNX2 was not perturbed, its protein was not measured, and no ChIP, reporter or direct WWOX-RUNX2 interaction assay was performed. The RUNX2 bridge is INFERENZA, not direct mechanism.

THE INTRATIBIAL COMPARISON HAS UNEQUAL ENDPOINTS. HOS-EV animals were sacrificed at about three weeks and HOS-WWOX animals at five weeks to reach comparable primary size. LM7 formed no intratibial tumours in the interval and therefore contributes no intratibial metastasis result.

THE LM7 INTRAVENOUS PANEL PRINTS p=0.05 WHILE METHODS DEFINE SIGNIFICANCE AS P<0.05. Without an unrounded value the displayed comparison is boundary evidence. Figure 4 has no visible significance marks or biological replicate count, and LM7 integrin alpha-2 is not visibly reduced, so the broad all-targets wording was not adopted.

🔴 WWOX HAS ONE FUNCTIONAL PPXY-BINDING DOMAIN, NOT TWO, AND IT IS MEASURED. The isolated WW2 domain shows NO detectable interaction with any of the five PPXY motifs across WBP1 and WBP2 — and the result is not one assay but ITC, a GST pulldown in HEK293 cells, CD, DSC and structural modelling agreeing, with the structural reason given: R25/W44 in WW1 are replaced by E66/Y85 in WW2, and an E66R/Y85W double substitution restores binding.

AND THE AFFINITIES ARE WEAK, WHICH 'physiologically-relevant micromolar range' DOES NOT CONVEY. Table 1, isolated WW1: WBP2_PY3 at 122 ± 1 μM, WBP1_PY2 at 366 ± 23 μM, NO BINDING DETECTED for the other three motifs — three of five PPXY motifs in two genuine adaptor proteins are not bound at all. Binding is enthalpy-driven with unfavourable entropy. INFERENZA: 122 μM is a transient, high-turnover contact, and any model in which WWOX HOLDS a partner in the cytoplasm has to explain how an interaction this weak holds anything.

🔴 AND THE TANDEM BINDS ONE PEPTIDE, NOT TWO — WHICH CORRECTS AN INFERENCE I RECORDED YESTERDAY. Table 5: the wild-type WW1-WW2 tandem binds WBP2_PY3 with fitted stoichiometry n = 1.05 ± 0.01 at Kd 49 ± 1 μM, and WBP1_PY2 at n = 0.99 ± 0.04. ONE LIGAND PER TANDEM. Only the ENGINEERED WW1-WW2rw tandem, with WW2's binding chemistry restored, reaches n = 2.00. Adjudicating PMID 16061658 yesterday I recorded the authors' hypothesis that WWOX out-binds YAP 'due to the interaction of WWOX with BOTH the PPxY motifs of ErbB-4' and carried it forward as 'two contacts against one — the competition is asymmetric'. THAT MECHANISM IS NOW MEASURED AND IT IS NOT TWO CONTACTS. Aqeilan's own word was 'perhaps' and I recorded the hedge with it; what is corrected is my restatement, not their claim.

WHAT SURVIVES IS AN AFFINITY ADVANTAGE, NOT A VALENCY ADVANTAGE, AND IT IS REAL. WW1 alone binds WBP2_PY3 at 122 μM; the tandem binds it at 49 μM — better than two-fold. And the tandem acquires binding to WBP2_PY2, which WW1 alone does not detectably bind: the authors call it an increased capture radius. So the second WW domain matters, by making the first one tighter and broader rather than by adding a site. Mechanistically a different claim from the one this corpus was carrying, and the one the data support.

AND THE STRUCTURAL SURPRISE THAT EXPLAINS IT: THE BINDING DOMAIN IS THE DISORDERED ONE. WW1, which binds, is largely unstructured and folds on ligand binding — heat-capacity change of about −120 cal/mol/K alone against less than −10 in the tandem, meaning it is already folded there. WW2, which binds nothing, is a well-folded β-sheet melting about 7°C higher. The authors state the lesson themselves: lack of structure does not equate to lack of binding, nor the reverse. INFERENZA FOR THE REFERENCE GENOTYPE: a missense variant in WW1 sits in an intrinsically disordered segment that folds only on engagement, so predicting its effect from a static structure predicts the wrong state — the same caution PMID 30356099 raised from the clinical side when it recorded that every missense call in the largest WOREE cohort rests on in silico prediction.

🔴 AND A FINDING THIS CORPUS DID NOT KNOW IT NEEDED: A SEQUENCE-LEVEL BASIS FOR THE WWOX-ITCH COMPETITION, FROM 2012. Searching the human proteome for WW domains carrying an arginine and a tryptophan at the positions that make WW1 a binder returns only a handful — AND EVERY ONE BELONGS TO THE E3 UBIQUITIN LIGASE FAMILY, NAMING ITCH AND NEDD4. WWOX's binding domain shares its recognition signature specifically with the ligases whose substrates it is later shown to contest. The arc this corpus holds — 'WWOX competes with ITCH on ΔNp63α' from PMID 23370280, 2013 — is an OBSERVATION; this paper predates it and supplies a reason the observation should have been expected. It does NOT make ITCH selectivity a DATO: nothing here manipulates ITCH, and the authors offer the consequence as 'we are tempted to suggest'. It moves the competition from coincidence to prediction.

THE RECOGNITION MOTIF IS LONGER THAN PPXY, WHICH CHANGES WHAT COUNTS AS A BINDING SITE. Alanine scanning shows proline at −2 and tyrosine at +4 are required for high affinity, making PXPPXYY the optimal consensus rather than minimal PPXY. PRACTICAL FORCE: any inventory of 'WWOX partners' built by scanning proteomes for PPXY overstates the set, and this paper demonstrates it — three of five motifs in two genuine adaptors are not bound.

AND AQEILAN, A CO-AUTHOR HERE, FRAMES THE WWOX-YAP COMPETITION AS AN OPEN QUESTION IN 2012, SEVEN YEARS AFTER THE PAPER I ADJUDICATED YESTERDAY: 'the ability OR LACK THEREOF of WWOX to compete with YAP for cellular partners may be a defining event'. That is the strongest available evidence that the 2005 hedge — 'WWOX and YAP MAY compete' — was meant, and was still meant seven years later by the same author.
